clue.text: What churchmen assume will take the lead

definitions.text: What churchmen assume will take the lead

parts.words: What churchmen assume will take the lead
parts.note: clergy put on a white band at the neck, and the same kind of band on a pet is what a leash clips onto

explanation.surface: A remark that clergymen expect to be in charge of proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the lead' reads as being in front, but it means having a dog's leash attached; 'assume' means put on, as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white clerical band worn by priests shares its name with the strap round a pet's neck.

clue.text: Curtains in short supply, lacking rayon primarily

indicators.note: lacking tells us a letter is dropped from the word for scarcity

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity, a state of short supply

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word rayon

explanation.surface: Drapes that are hard to come by because the synthetic fabric has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' looks like window drapes, but it is slang for the end of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains is informal slang for the end, as in 'it's curtains for him', meaning demise.

clue.text: Good girl on trial that's just for show

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A virtuous young woman in court whose prosecution is mere theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A display cabinet with transparent panels exists only to exhibit its contents to viewers.

clue.text: Man on boundary with rifle, due to get replacement

indicators.note: the letters are replaced in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man stationed at a border with a gun, about to be relieved by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundary' suggests a frontier guard, but in cricket the boundary is the edge of the field, where fielders stand deep.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket or baseball, a fielder placed far from the batter, near the edge of the field.

clue.text: General hospital area away from the weather

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A military leader in a hospital unit sheltered from storms.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side is the sheltered side, facing away from the wind and weather.

clue.text: Absolute fortune to share out again

parts.note: real can mean absolute, as in a real disaster
one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone's entire wealth to be divided up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute shares; doing it once more redistributes the portions.

clue.text: Namely, how to move a trailer

definitions.meaning: a formal phrase meaning that is to say
you pull the caravan behind your car: haul the thing

explanation.surface: An instruction specifying the method of shifting a caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal phrase meaning 'that is to say', and literally the instruction to pull something behind a vehicle.

clue.text: Subject once paired with art

parts.note: an archaic second-person pronoun in the subject position went with the old verb form art, as in the old phrase meaning 'you are'

explanation.surface: A school subject historically taught alongside art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a school subject; it is the grammatical subject, and 'art' is the old form of 'are'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic pronoun for 'you' took the verb form 'art', as in 'wherefore art'.

clue.text: Wife cut one's share

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A spouse reduces someone's portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, your whack is your fair portion, as in paying the full amount.

clue.text: Tribal divisions, basically

parts.note: tribalism at root splits people into two camps, our side versus the other side

explanation.surface: A summary of how tribes split into groups.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sums up an us-versus-the-others mentality, the basic split behind tribal loyalty.

clue.text: A short celebration on one's own

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word for the celebration

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: A brief festivity enjoyed by oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Separately, alone, at a distance from others: 'living apart' means on one's own.

clue.text: Fancy detail

definitions.meaning: verb: to explain more fully, expand on

explanation.surface: An intricate small particular.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means ornate and intricate; as a verb it means to expand on in detail.

clue.text: Friendly sort of shop, one with food

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the word shop is rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
table can mean the food provided, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A welcoming kind of store offering a single meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Welcoming and generous to guests is the core sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Seabirds return to find another

indicators.note: return means the word for these birds is read backwards

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as puffins

explanation.surface: Seagulls come back and discover a fellow bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'another' means another seabird, leaning on the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: This predatory gull-like bird is another kind of seabird, as the clue's opening word implies.

clue.text: Blair clashes with Iran's bookkeepers

indicators.note: clashes suggests the letters are thrown into conflict and jumbled

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister quarrels with a Middle Eastern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookkeepers' suggests accountants, but it is literal: people who keep books. Blair is Tony Blair, UK prime minister 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Library staff literally keep books, so the accountancy word is read at face value.

clue.text: Not running, like horses in the stable

definitions.meaning: of an engine or a process, having stopped
put into stalls, as horses are housed

explanation.surface: Horses kept indoors are not out racing.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that has cut out has stopped, and horses kept in stalls are housed this way.

clue.text: Stand firm, partly thanks to new alliance

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Hold your ground, in part because of a fresh coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or resist obstinately is to keep a defiant position without yielding.

clue.text: Part of chicken swallowed by boy caused slight pain

indicators.note: swallowed by means the chicken part goes inside the boy's name

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
a wing is a part of a chicken

explanation.surface: A lad eating a piece of poultry got a pang.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp little pain, so this past-tense verb means gave a mild pang.

clue.text: Inadvisable subject for oral examination

parts.note: from the proverb about not looking a present animal in the mouth, as checking its teeth tells its age

explanation.surface: A topic you shouldn't pick for a spoken test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examination' suggests a viva; it is literal, inspecting a mouth. The proverb says don't look a free animal in the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against checking the teeth of a present, so this is the thing not to examine orally.

clue.text: Two bats in demand at picnics

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the pair of batters who start the innings
bottle and tin tools needed outdoors

explanation.surface: A pair of cricket bats are popular at outdoor meals.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first two batsmen in are the openers; at a picnic you need tools for bottles and tins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's first-wicket batting pair and devices for uncorking or unsealing share this plural name.

clue.text: It has us squirming, this massage

indicators.note: squirming means the letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: A massage that makes us wriggle about.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese therapy using finger pressure on points of the body, a type of massage.

clue.text: Transport may be safe with these glass bottles

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

indicators.note: may be signals the letters of safe could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Vehicles can be secure when carrying these glass vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass vessels with flared necks used to serve wine or water at table.

clue.text: Esoteric organisation? Certainly, second left

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of esoteric are reorganised

explanation.surface: Asking about a secret society and being directed to take the second turning on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ESOTERIC with S (second) left out; 'Certainly' is the reply to the question, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small exclusive circle with shared, often obscure interests is an esoteric organisation.

clue.text: God who's angry when rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the word for angry is turned back

parts.note: sore means angry, chiefly in US usage

explanation.surface: A deity who becomes furious on being spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love, son of Aphrodite, counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Promises of loyalty host makes at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every second letter of these two words is taken

explanation.surface: Pledges of allegiance that a host gives periodically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promises of loyalty' looks like the whole definition, but 'of loyalty' supplies letters: the even letters of LOYALTY HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn vows or sworn pledges are promises made formally.

clue.text: Imagine that! Going topless in fancy headgear

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word that is removed

explanation.surface: Amazing: someone stripping off while wearing an elaborate hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed decorated hat for women, as seen in portraits, is a showy piece of headwear.

clue.text: Newspaper article leads with crime

indicators.note: leads with means the article comes before the newspaper

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A press story opens with a criminal offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, the paper this crossword appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a crime, so the offence of stealing fits.

clue.text: Abridged contents of magazine

parts.note: a gun's magazine holds cartridges, and the short form of the word for those bullets is a clipped word

explanation.surface: A shortened table of contents for a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' looks like a periodical, but it is the part of a gun that holds bullets; 'Abridged' says the word is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for ammunition, the cartridges held in a firearm's magazine.

clue.text: Pilot's instrument change takes time

indicators.note: takes means the word for change holds the word time inside it

parts.note: to alter is to change
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviator's device for change requires time.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft gauge measuring height above sea level, used by pilots.

clue.text: Not quite a colour match

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped from the colour

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: Something that almost matches in shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond or tally, as stories or accounts that match each other.

clue.text: Western cowcatcher, possibly

parts.note: in a cowboy film, a rope noose is what literally catches cattle

explanation.surface: Perhaps the guard on the front of an American Western locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: A cowcatcher is the frame on the front of a train; here it is read literally, something that catches cows in a Western.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rope with a running noose that cowboys throw to catch cattle.

clue.text: A foreign asset maybe gets one extremely nervous

parts.note: une is French for a

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters could be in another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A holding abroad perhaps makes someone very jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of anxious or ill at ease, meaning most nervous.
